correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 and positive two-class prices and budget, the explicit centered 2m-point circular embedding has edge-chord squared lengths precisely equal to the alternating prices. The Rayleigh trace bounds the spectral gap of every independent nonnegative-edge design by B/(2mR^2). The stated strictly positive rates satisfy the budget and the two-dimensional eigenvector equilibrium; the exact Bloch decomposition proves their common eigenvalue is lambda_2. An equal-value competitor must satisfy the same vector equilibrium at every vertex; independent consecutive chords then force each incident conductance to match. The m=2 and equal-price boundaries and the size-response statements are handled algebraically. Actual verify.py reported PASS on 842 assertions, including rational spectra for 4 and 6 vertices; sampling is not an infinite proof.

The 2007 Boyd-Diaconis-Parrilo-Xiao paper optimizes a different discrete-time SLEM and treats standard cycles. The result makes no novelty claim for the generic SDP, Bloch eigenvalue formula, or polygon dual technique. Targeted published-source and mathematical-finding searches did not identify coverage of the whole new claim; unindexed equivalences remain possible.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural continuous-time Markov/consensus mixing-rate design for alternating per-unit-cost links. The theorem solves an infinite family with all edge conductances individually free, produces exact unique resource shares and mixing rate, identifies a nontrivial four-cycle price-response exception, and yields a strict finite-size interpolation to square-root price allocation. It is not merely the eigenvalues of fixed weights or an arbitrarily chosen finite case. The independent conductance optimality and uniqueness avoid solving the generic SDP repeatedly.
